claim: Dbx1-derived pre-Bötzinger complex neurons are critical for rhythm generation.
source: Recently, we established in vitro that Dbx1-derived pre-Bötzinger complex neurons are critical for rhythm generation and that a subpopulation serves a premotor function (Wang et al., 2014).

claim: A subpopulation of Dbx1-derived pre-Bötzinger complex neurons serves a premotor function.

claim: A subpopulation of Dbx1-derived intermediate reticular (IRt) neurons are rhythmically active during inspiration.
source: Here, we further show that a subpopulation of Dbx1-derived intermediate reticular (IRt) neurons are rhythmically active during inspiration and project to the hypoglossal (XII) nucleus that contains motoneurons important for maintaining airway patency.
evidence: Supported by experimental data from recordings shown in the manuscript

claim: Dbx1-derived IRt neurons project to the hypoglossal (XII) nucleus.

evidence: Supported by experimental data including antidromic activation and anatomical reconstruction

claim: The hypoglossal nucleus contains motoneurons important for maintaining airway patency.
source: Here, we further show that a subpopulation of Dbx1-derived intermediate reticular (IRt) neurons are rhythmically active during inspiration and project to the hypoglossal (XII) nucleus that contains motoneurons important for maintaining airway patency.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about XII motoneurons

claim: 57% of Dbx1 IRt neurons are glutamatergic.
source: Laser ablation of Dbx1 IRt neurons, 57% of which are glutamatergic, decreased ipsilateral inspiratory motor output without affecting frequency.
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data presented in the manuscript

claim: Laser ablation of Dbx1 IRt neurons decreased ipsilateral inspiratory motor output.

claim: Laser ablation of Dbx1 IRt neurons did not affect inspiratory frequency.

claim: A subset of Dbx1 IRt neurons is a source of premotor excitatory drive contributing to the inspiratory behavior of XII motoneurons.
source: We conclude that a subset of Dbx1 IRt neurons is a source of premotor excitatory drive, contributing to the inspiratory behavior of XII motoneurons, as well as a key component of the airway control network whose dysfunction contributes to sleep apnea.
evidence: Conclusion based on experimental data from recordings and ablations

claim: Dbx1 IRt neurons are a key component of the airway control network whose dysfunction contributes to sleep apnea.
source: We conclude that a subset of Dbx1 IRt neurons is a source of premotor excitatory drive, contributing to the inspiratory behavior of XII motoneurons, as well as a key component of the airway control network whose dysfunction contributes to sleep apnea.
evidence: Inference based on experimental findings and known role of airway control in sleep apnea

claim: Central pattern generator circuits comprise rhythmogenic and pattern-forming components that underlie rhythmic behaviors including breathing, locomotion, and mastication.

claim: Of 2777 lacZ-labeled cells counted along the length of the medullary IRt in four animals, 1591 cells co-localized Slc17a6.

evidence: Supported by experimental cell counting data shown in Figure 1B-D

claim: 57 ± 1% of Dbx1 IRt neurons are glutamatergic.
